newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares continue slide on low demand. [corrected 18:30 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares continue slide on low demand. [corrected 18:30 gmt]

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued to slide on Thursday, with most buyers feeling the waters as the market passes through a traditionally slow spell, brokers said.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its overall index fell 5.44 points to 378.68. Volume was unusually high at 288.86 million pounds ($85.08 million), most of it in Egyptian Lebanese for the Production of Tiles and Sanitary Ware/Lecico.
Lecico traded in more than 230 million pounds and closed 30.45 (corrects from 304.5) pounds higher at 639.5. Broker Dalia Sultan of EFG/Hermes said a board member had sold his shares.
Earlier this month the Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab said its Sanitec Oy Ltd bathroom porcelain unit and Sanitec's Lebanese partners would acquire 75 percent control of Lecico.
Tobacco firm Eastern Company was the day's second most active share, trading in more than 13.00 million pounds but ended 0.92 pounds lower at 17.58.
"Eastern's price has gone down and it is an attractive stock," Sultan said of the company's performance.
She said many other stocks had gone down on poor demand but the slide would attract investors seeking low prices.
"The market is traditionally slow in March and April in Cairo. I expect it to start picking up in May. Don't ask me why," Sultan said.
Helwan Portland Cement was the busiest of the cement bunch, trading in more than three million pounds but it closed unchanged at 79.00.

More than 2.5 million pounds changed hands in Egyptian Tora Portland Cement but it too closed unchanged at 98.00. Suez Cement slipped 0.55 pounds to close at 69.25 after trading in more than 2.10 million pounds and Amriyah Cement traded in more than two million pounds but slipped 1.25 pounds to close at 83.00. "The cement sector as a whole is very attractive," Sultan said.
Fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial lost 5.00 pounds to close at 195 after more than 2.10 million pounds were traded.
Popular real estate stock Medinet Nasr Housing and Development rose 3.51 pounds to end trading at 468.51 after shares worth more than 3.20 million pounds changed hands.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 594.44 from 610.81 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 259.44 points from 261.2.
Out of the 92 shares traded, 22 gained, 46 lost and 24 ended the day unchanged.
